_comment: Settled questions about the Lease Comps book, in machine-readable form.
The problem this solves: a blank cell cannot tell you whether nobody has answered the
question or whether JD answered it and the answer was 'unknown'. Prose in the research
queue was the only record of the difference, and prose drifts — on 2026-09-06 the queue
claimed 8 turnkey comps sat on the benchmark when the real number was 10, and a re-run of
the flat-rent audit would have re-raised 13 leases JD had already confirmed as flat.
tools/sheet_ops/audit.py reads this file and suppresses settled findings, so an agent or a
human running the audit sees only what is genuinely open. Add a decision here at the same
time you apply it to the workbook. Never delete one to make a finding reappear — if a
decision is wrong, change the ruling and say why.

conventions.turnkey_benchmark_note: Standing estimate where JD has no real figure. An owner-supplied number always wins.

building_ti.ruling: Any raw space at 360 PAS takes the turnkey value Rogo actually negotiated. Second-generation space falls outside the rule.
60 Madison turnkey deals take $110/SF, from Pace.
building_ti.caveat: Pace's $110 was a Second Gen installation; Tenex (LC-0003) is Raw, and a raw build normally costs more. Replace if a real Tenex figure surfaces.

settled.ruling: These leases run longer than five years and genuinely carry no escalation. A blank Rent P2 is the answer, not a gap. Do not re-raise.

Custom build-outs whose layout the tenant's own real estate team set. JD has no visibility and none is obtainable. Leave blank — never estimate. A guessed seat count on a 462,000 SF comp would move the Dashboard cost/seat further than any real number in the book.
Confirmed at $150/SF as a real figure, not the benchmark standing in for an unknown. The number is unchanged; the point is that it is no longer an estimate.
A confirmed zero on an as-is deal is a real zero, not an unknown. Every comp here carries an As-Is delivery condition, so TI $0 and the delivery condition agree. Unknown TI is left blank instead.
Same tenant, same building, genuinely separate transactions — an initial deal and a later expansion, on different floors and different dates. Comps stay one row per transaction and are never merged.

Building-level submarket rulings on the record: 1 Madison Avenue is PAS / Mad. Square Park; 675 Avenue of the Americas is Flatiron; 837 Washington Street is Meatpacking; the whole Penn cluster (2/5/21 Penn Plaza, 330 West 34th, 1245 and 1375 Broadway) is Hudson Yards / Penn Station. 'SoHo' and 'Soho/Noho' merged to 'SoHo/NoHo'. Chelsea/Meatpacking and Penn Station retired from Reference.
Midtown and NoMad are kept in Reference with no comps on purpose — they are real submarkets that future deals will land in.

open.why: Tempo Labs is held on the $150 benchmark deliberately. It already carries an unverified Seed round (the entire Seed cohort, n=1); guessing its TI would compound one open question with another.

No TIA figure, so no NER is computed and the comp sits out of every average. Blank is correct per the contract. LC-0096 (Mirage) additionally carries an As-Is delivery condition, which normally implies a confirmed $0 rather than an unknown — worth resolving one way or the other.

Tempus has no TIA figure, so its delivery condition cannot be stated either — As-Is, Custom TIA and LL Turnkey each assert something about an allowance nobody knows. Blank is the honest entry until a real TI number surfaces, at which point both fields get filled together.
